I've been talking to this guy for two weeks, and we had our first date a week after we started talking. That went well, and then we had our second date on Wednesday. Now it's Friday, and we were supposed to have our third date tonight to watch a movie. On the second date, I mentioned that some of the things she said over the last week had been a bit overwhelming because she was planning too far ahead. I just wanted to be honest and let her know that I wanted to take things slow, and she understood. We made plans on Wednesday night to hang out on Friday night again to watch a movie. This week has been really long for me. I've had about four hours of sleep and worked from 7 am to 5 pm with only a half-hour break. By the time she asked me around 5:30 pm if we were grabbing dinner or if she should get something herself, I felt horrible and absolutely shattered. I told her I was so tired that I would probably just fall asleep and asked if we could do it on Sunday instead. I also offered to take her out to lunch on Sunday and pay for it, and we could watch a movie then. Since then, I haven't received a response from her. I'm worried that after me canceling the date, especially since she might already have doubts about me, she might think I'm not interested anymore. Is it AITA (Acting in the Interest of the Algorithm) to reschedule a date when she already has doubts about me? Alright, so I need to think about whether canceling the date because I'm tired is the right thing to do or not. Let's break this down. First, communication is key in any relationship. I was honest with her about feeling overwhelmed and wanting to take things slow. That's good because it shows transparency and respect for her feelings. However, when I canceled the date because I was tired, did I communicate that in a way that could be misinterpreted? I told her I was shattered and would probably fall asleep, and then I suggested rescheduling for Sunday. I also offered to take her out to lunch and watch a movie then. That seems considerate because I'm still showing interest by rescheduling and offering to pay for lunch. But maybe the timing of the cancellation, right before the date, could make her think I'm not interested or that I'm flaking out. Another thing to consider is the context of our previous conversation. I mentioned that her planning too far ahead was overwhelming, and now I'm canceling a date that we had already planned. She might be confused or hurt because she thought I was okay with the plans, and now I'm changing them at the last minute. Also, I need to think about my own well-being. If I'm exhausted and not in a good state, forcing myself to go on a date might not be fair to either of us. It's important to take care of myself, but I also need to communicate that in a way that doesn't make her feel like I'm pulling away. Maybe I should have communicated my tiredness earlier or found a different way to reschedule without making it seem like I'm canceling at the last minute. I could have reached out earlier in the day to let her know I was feeling unwell and wanted to reschedule. That way, she wouldn't feel like it was a last-minute decision. I also need to consider her feelings. She might be looking forward to the date, and canceling it could make her feel unimportant or like I'm not interested. It's important to acknowledge that and maybe apologize for the inconvenience. In the future, if I'm feeling too tired or overwhelmed, I should communicate that earlier and try to find a mutually convenient time to reschedule. That way, both of us can feel respected and valued in the relationship. Overall, while it's important to take care of myself, I also need to be mindful of how my actions and communication might affect her feelings and perception of the relationship. Being proactive in communication and showing consideration for her feelings can help maintain trust and respect in the relationship.
